title: Underived open-composition and restriction models respect counits
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq Y$ an arbitrary open, $V=h^{-1}U$, $g:V\to U$ and $j_X,j_Y$ the open inclusions. On homotopy categories of module complexes let $\alpha_0:h_*r_Y\cong r_Xg_*$ and $\beta_0:j_{X*}h_*\cong g_*j_{Y*}$ be the fixed models [def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-open-counit-model], with open adjunction counits $\varepsilon_X,\varepsilon_Y$ [def-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-data]. For every homotopy object K on V, $r_Y(\beta_{0,K});\varepsilon_{Y,g_*K}=\alpha_{0,j_{X*}K};g_*(\varepsilon_{X,K})$. This is an underived sectionwise identity: no derived category, derived comparison or derived adjunction is involved.

source.place: Tags 08FE, 0D5T and 08BV; official pages https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08FE, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D5T and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08BV, read 2026-10-14

proof.text: Use schemeMVOrdinaryOpenCounit_square for the fixed ordinary-module comparisons and open adjunctions. This isolates the sectionwise restriction calculation from the passage to complexes and the homotopy category.

In the fully proved private helper lift_open_counit_square, choose a complex M with quotient image K. Rewrite the two localized counits using Adjunction.mapHomotopyCategory_counit_app_quotient. The fixed homotopy comparison components and maps of quotient morphisms are quotient images of their termwise counterparts. Combine the two quotient images using Functor.map_comp, and reduce equality of complex maps to equality of their degree-n components. The mapHomologicalComplex composition-isomorphism formulas and counit formula reduce this precisely to the ordinary counit square at M.X n. Cancel the identity composition factors and apply that ordinary equality.

Specialize the private helper to the two open adjunctions and the fixed underived restriction/composition isomorphisms. Explicitly type the adjunction right functors as RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage to match the additive instances and the public homotopy models. This gives the existing theorem with its statement unchanged.
